basics.name: Baidu Li
basics.label: Machine Learning Engineer · Medical AI
basics.summary: Biomedical engineering and computer science background, with experience in 3D medical imaging, model interpretability, foundation-model evaluation, LLM agents, RAG, and research automation.

work.name: UHN AI Hub — University Health Network
work.summary: Medical imaging, foundation-model evaluation, and agent-driven research workflows.
highlights: Coordinator for the CVPR 2026 3D CT Foundation Model (3DCTFM) competition. Worked on cross-anatomy CT benchmarking, including data preparation and splits, model execution, metrics, automated evaluation scripts, and result and error analysis.
Developed a Multi-Head nnU-Net framework for complex 3D tumor segmentation.
Built an nnU-Net data-conversion agent and an HPC cluster-management tool for Slurm job execution on Compute Canada.
Contributing to a clinical-note generation prototype that combines referral letters, patient information, and processed text conversations. My work focuses on the text-conversation input.

work.name: SpringBorne Life Science
work.summary: AI/ML medical-device guidance, software validation, and documentation automation.
highlights: Authored guidance on AI/ML-enabled medical devices, covering risk management, algorithm selection, and mitigation strategies in the context of FDA draft guidance and ISO standards.
Developed software validation plans to support work involving ISO 13485 and 21 CFR Part 11.
Implemented a Neo4j document relationship network for design control and developed a no-code AI platform for standardized compliance-report generation.

work.name: XtalPi
work.summary: Agent toolsets and RAG workflows for life-sciences research.
highlights: Extended the Dify agent framework with tools for research literature review and data analysis.
Processed and cleaned RAG datasets and built domain-specific retrieval workflows with Dify and PostgreSQL.
Designed an agent toolset framework to connect research tasks with reusable tools.

work.name: York University
work.summary: Deep learning for software testing, advised by Dr. Song Wang.
highlights: Led a team developing a deep-learning approach to improve the efficiency of a fuzz-testing framework.

awards.title: autoPET V — 3rd place in both tasks
awards.summary: Competed as the sole member of FightTumor. Built a GPT-agent-driven workflow in which agents implemented the code and executed 100+ experiments on a single RTX 5090.

projects.name: autoPET V · FightTumor
projects.summary: Solo entrant, ranked 3rd in both tasks. Built a GPT-agent-driven workflow in which agents implemented the code and executed 100+ experiments on a single RTX 5090.

projects.name: From Pixels to Patients
projects.summary: Independently authored an interactive lung-CT interpretability tutorial listed in the MICCAI Educational Challenge 2026 library. Compared seven attribution approaches, including a mean-activation baseline, on five LUNA25 examples using a published JSC model, with real 3D feature visualizations, lesion-localization metrics, and reproducibility records.

projects.name: CT Foundation-Model Benchmarking
projects.summary: Coordinated the CVPR 2026 3DCTFM competition and worked on data splits, model runs, metrics, automated evaluation, and error analysis across anatomical regions at UHN.

projects.name: Multi-Head nnU-Net
projects.summary: Developed a Multi-Head nnU-Net framework for complex 3D tumor segmentation at UHN, alongside data-conversion agents and HPC/Slurm research tools.

projects.name: Clinical Note Generation
projects.summary: Contributing to a UHN prototype that combines referral letters, patient information, and processed text conversations into consultation notes. My work focuses on the text-conversation input.

projects.name: Research Agents & RAG
projects.summary: Extended Dify agent tools and built domain-specific retrieval workflows at XtalPi, supporting literature review and data analysis for life-sciences research.

projects.name: AI-Assisted Compliance
projects.summary: Built a Neo4j relationship network for design-control documents and an AI-assisted compliance-report platform at SpringBorne, connecting regulatory research with practical software tools.
